reflections.summary: We won the series by consistently stacking Spikes with Hisuian Samurott and using Dragapult and Incineroar to pivot and control the pace. The opponent lacked hazard removal, so repeated entry damage from Spikes wore down their frail offensive core. Serperior pressured Arcanine and Grimmsnarl, while Mega Gengar was handled by sacrificing Serperior and finishing with Samurott. The team-preview plan of bringing four without Mega Gardevoir was correct, as Samurott's Dark/Water coverage and hazard stacking proved more reliable against Mega Gengar's speed. Between-game adjustments were not shown, but the same approach worked for both games.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, keep the same four (Incineroar, Dragapult, Serperior, Samurott). Consider Mega Gardevoir over Serperior for immediate Fairy-type pressure, but Serperior’s Contrary-boosted Leaf Storm was effective and it can be used as bait for Mega Gengar's Sludge Bomb. If bringing Mega Gardevoir, must pair it with speed control or redirection to handle Gengar safely.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core: Arcanine (Intimidate, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, Flamethrower, Sitrus Berry, Calm), Grimmsnarl (Fake Out, Sucker Punch, Taunt, Protect, Colbur Berry, Impish), Empoleon (Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Flash Cannon, Protect, Chople Berry, Torrent, Calm), Mega Gengar (Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Thunderbolt, Protect, Timid). Leads Arcanine + Grimmsnarl, pivots to Empoleon and Gengar. No hazard removal—Spikes from Ceaseless Edge are crippling. Grimmsnarl’s Taunt and Sucker Punch attempt to disrupt, but Fake Out can flinch it. Empoleon often Protects early, so call out or double-target when it’s vulnerable. Mega Gengar is the main speed threat; Dragapult outspeeds and OHKOes with Shadow Ball, or Samurott’s Ceaseless Edge after chip. Slowbro and Bastiodon were not brought, likely preferring offense; if brought, Bastiodon’s Wide Guard does not block Ceaseless Edge, but Stealth Rock may be set. Our pivoting (U-turn, Parting Shot) and speed advantage are key; Serperior snowballs but must avoid Sludge Bomb. Samurott’s Sharpness-boosted Aqua Cutter/Sacred Sword provide strong coverage; Ceaseless Edge is a win condition.

reflections.summary: Lost game2 and series 0-2 due to team-preview mismatch: brought Mega Gengar (evolved) which is weak to Samurott-Hisui's Dark Ceaseless Edge and Dragapult's Ghost coverage; opponent's Dark/Water/Fighting attacks exploited our types. Between-game adjustment to include and Mega Evolve Gengar backfired—it removed Serperior but was immediately revenge-killed, costing momentum. Prep correctly gave Empoleon Chople Berry vs Fighting and Arcanine Intimidate, but registered six lacked bench bulk (Slowbro/Bastiodon) to withstand opponent's pivot pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Future vs this opponent: avoid Mega Gengar unless protected; use Bastiodon or Slowbro from registered pool for Dark/Water resist. Keep Empoleon+Grimmsnarl lead but don't switch Gengar into spikes. Do not evolve Gengar against Dark-heavy teams. Build more Fighting/Dark-resistant sets; respect opponent's U-turn/Parting Shot pivots.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core: Incineroar (Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, FlareBlitz/ThroatChop) + Dragapult (Timid LifeOrb, U-turn, Shadow Ball) lead. Samurott-Hisui (Adamant Sharpness FocusSash) Ceaseless Edge (Dark, 2x Ghost) + Sacred Sword (Fighting, 2x Steel) + Aqua Cutter; loves Protect. Serperior (Contrary Timid Leftovers) Leaf Storm self-boosts SpA+2, Taunt/Protect. Unseen: Kingambit (Adamant BlackGlasses SuckerPunch/KowtowCleave/IronHead), Gardevoir (Timid Gardevoirite HyperVoice/Psychic/WillOWisp). Strategic facts: they pivot with U-turn/Parting Shot to gain advantage; Spikes on our side hurt our own switches. Prep conclusions: Empoleon Chople good vs Samurott Fighting; Arcanine Intimidate helpful but frail; Grimmsnarl Prankster Taunt blocked by Protect; never bring Ghost vs their Dark; bench bulk mons was error; keep Mega stone unused if opponent has Dark coverage.
